messages:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a burst of inference pods scheduled to gpu-pool-usw2 that either get preempted immediately or hang in Terminating while CA spins up spot nodes. Started ~09:12 UTC and still noisy. Anyone digging into taints/tolerations side of things?

olivia: Yep saw the alerts. Sequence looks like: node becomes NotReady -> CA drains -> new spot node joins -> pods stuck because tolerationSeconds expired during drain. The sidecar injection seems to set a toleration with no tolerationSeconds so pod is evicted immediately once taint applied.

matt: Dumping a relevant log chunk we pulled from kube-scheduler/ca events: 
```
I0318 09:12:33.123  kube-scheduler ] Binding pod inference-abc to node/gpu-spot-42
I0318 09:12:34.001  kubelet ] Node gpu-spot-42 NotReady - network flaps
I0318 09:12:34.002  evictions ] Evicting pod inference-abc due to taint: accelerator=exclusive:NoSchedule
I0318 09:12:34.500  ca       ] Scale-up: need 2 nodes; provisioning spot-usw2-c
```
matt: The taint in our node bootstrap is `accelerator=exclusive:NoSchedule` and the pod toleration we inject is just the generic Exists toleration. That means on taint application kubelet/eviction logic doesn't wait — eviction can still happen fast.

rina: We historically relied on tolerationSeconds for graceful eviction in cases of transient network blips so inference pods can finish in-flight work. Current sidecar injector YAML fragment looks like: 
```
      tolerations:
      - key: "accelerator"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```
rina: No tolerationSeconds here. If CA is draining because node NotReady then evictions are immediate. For spot nodes we should maybe set tolerationSeconds: 120-300 so short blips don't cause full restart.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] cluster-autoscaler/usw2 triggered scale-up to 2 nodes at 2026-03-18T09:12:34Z — reason: insufficient cpu/gpu for deployment/inference-service-prod.

jay: Two tradeoffs to consider: 1) increasing tolerationSeconds reduces immediate preemptions and request retries but holds onto spot node capacity longer (cost). 2) setting tolerationSeconds interacts badly with CA scale-down: if pods tolerate taint for a long time CA might delay removing nodes even when they're underutilized.

sam: Cost hit is my worry. For high-throughput inference we can't have many long-lived nodes idle. Could we target only critical pods (latency p99) to have longer toleration and leave batch jobs default?

olivia: Yes — we can add a label + mutating webhook rule so only pods with label `inference.redwood/hold-while-unready=true` get tolerationSeconds: 300. Others get shorter or none. That way we limit cost exposure.

matt: Also worth adjusting nodeAffinity so inference pods prefer dedicated-on-demand pool for steady traffic and only spill to spot pool as overflow. Example preference: 
```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: nodepool-type
          operator: In
          values:
          - dedicated
```
matt: Combined with `max-surge`/`max-unavailable` on rollout it'll avoid thrashing during small flaps.

rina: There's another subtlety: CNI route setup delay after node join causes NodeReady false for ~10s, which combined with our quick eviction leads to flapping. We should tune kubelet node-status update and CNI warmup. I'll open a small runbook to test `--node-status-update-frequency` and a warmup init that waits for CNI.

sam: Plan summary?
- add label-driven tolerationSeconds for critical inference pods (rina to PR mutating webhook)
- prefer dedicated nodeAffinity for p99 routes (matt will add to helm chart)
- short-term tag spot pools as `scale-down-disabled` during peak windows to avoid churn (olivia will coordinate ops)
- run CNI warmup and kubelet status tests (rina)

jay: FWIW we should also add a CA expander rule: prefer on-demand for pods with `inference.redwood/hold-while-unready=true` so scale-up doesn't only create spot nodes. CA supports multiple node group priorities.

olivia: I'll schedule the canary change for the next maintenance window and watch token-level cost dashboard for the week. If p99 latency stays stable and cost delta < 8% we keep; else rollback.

sam: Sounds good. If anyone sees more Terminating/Failed pods in the next hour ping me and post pod names. Thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: I'll drop a quick checker script to look for pods with `accelerator` taint evicted within 30s of scheduling and post results here.

rina: I'll also add an e2e that simulates CNI delay and verifies tolerationSeconds behavior before we flip mutating webhook on prod.
